title: Ripple Responds to Critical XRP Bug That Threatened Fixed Supply
summary: XRP’s fixed supply faced a critical software threat that Ripple says was addressed before exploitation. Its engineering team is expanding AI-assisted testing and mathematical checks to uncover longstanding weaknesses as vulnerability discovery accelerates. Ripple Responds to a Threat to XRP’s Fixed ...
content:
XRP’s fixed supply faced a critical software threat that Ripple says was addressed before exploitation. Its engineering team is expanding AI-assisted testing and mathematical checks to uncover longstanding weaknesses as vulnerability discovery accelerates.

Key Takeaways

  • The bug could have created spendable XRP beyond its fixed supply.
  • The fix shipped Sept. 25; investigators found no evidence of exploitation.
  • Ripple is expanding simulated attacks and mathematical protocol checks.

Ripple Responds to a Threat to XRP’s Fixed Supply

A critical flaw could have allowed unauthorized XRP creation, prompting Ripple to reinforce security across the XRP Ledger (XRPL). J. Ayo Akinyele, senior director of engineering at RippleX, Ripple’s division supporting development of the public blockchain, outlined the response and security priorities on X on Oct. 10, following the vulnerability’s disclosure the previous day.

Veria AI, a vulnerability-detection system developed by security company Veria Labs, helped uncover the issue through the network’s bug bounty program, which rewards researchers for reporting weaknesses. Akinyele stated:

“The bug had existed in the codebase for over a decade and could have allowed XRP to be created beyond its fixed supply.”

That potential creation of unauthorized tokens threatened a limit established when all 100 billion XRP were created at the network’s inception. The XRP Ledger’s transaction system relies on validators agreeing on payment validity and order rather than mining new coins. Akinyele described developers thoroughly testing the patch and coordinating rapid upgrades with those operators before public disclosure.

How the Bug Could Have Created Unauthorized XRP

The payments engine could incorrectly calculate amounts owed across specially constructed trading offers, allowing sellers to receive more XRP than the buyer paid. The payments engine overflow flaw involved arithmetic exceeding its numerical limit and returning an incorrectly small total. The fix shipped Sept. 25 in xrpld 3.4.1, a release of the server software that processes transactions and maintains ledger records. Investigators found no evidence of public-network exploitation.

The discovery also sharpened Ripple’s focus on artificial intelligence and the need to identify weaknesses more quickly. The Ripple executive emphasized:

“AI is fundamentally changing how quickly vulnerabilities can be discovered.”

His response calls for stronger bounty programs, expanded AI-assisted searches, and adversarial testing, which simulates attacks to expose defects. An internal red team, consisting of specialists conducting controlled attacks, supports this work.

Those priorities build on Ripple’s proactive AI security efforts, including code scanning and reviews intended to detect problems earlier in development. Working with outside researchers and the XRPL Foundation, the team will revisit longstanding assumptions in payments, transaction agreement, and communication between servers. An updated assessment of potential threats will guide those examinations.

Ripple Targets Risks Beyond Individual Bugs

Ripple also intends to accelerate mathematical checks through its collaboration with Common Prefix, a blockchain research and development company, and the XRPL Foundation. Their work applies formal verification to XRP Ledger software to evaluate whether modeled behavior follows defined rules. Akinyele explained that this approach could uncover deeper issues other testing methods might miss.

Existing verification work on the Lending Protocol and Single Asset Vault will inform that expansion. The XRPL lending protocol design would handle loans and repayments on the ledger while borrower assessments occur outside it. Mainnet availability depends on activation of the required amendments, or network rule changes approved by validators.

The related vault is designed to pool one type of asset from depositors, supporting institutional capital pools on XRPL for lending and other functions. Akinyele tied growing financial-infrastructure use to greater responsibility and pledged continued investment with the community. He stressed:

“Our goal isn’t simply to find more bugs. It’s to systematically address the underlying risks and make the XRPL harder to exploit.”

title: XRP Ledger defends emergency patch for unlimited XRP bug
summary: The XRP Ledger Foundation pushed back against claims that its emergency security patch was forced on network operators.
content:
XRP Ledger developers have defended the emergency security patch used to fix a bug capable of creating XRP beyond the network’s fixed supply, saying they could not wait for the network’s usual two-week validator vote without exposing the flaw to attackers.

The fix, released on Sept. 25, came three days after a bug bounty report, and took effect immediately on any server that installed it. It was the first deliberate bypass of the normal amendment process since the system was introduced more than ten years ago, they said. 

“With a normal amendment vote, the fix would have been public for weeks before it took effect, risking network security,” XRPL developers said in an X post on Sunday. 

The expedited fix led to questions about XRPL’s level of decentralization. On its website, XRPL claims it is a fully decentralized, public blockchain — a characterization that has been central to arguments that its native token, XRP, is not a security. 

XRPL security fix “raised a lot of questions”

Cyber Capital founder Justin Bons said Thursday that marketing XRP to retail investors as decentralized amounted to “straight-up fraud.” He argued that the Sept. 25 emergency release shipped as binaries only, temporarily withheld the source code and pressured operators to upgrade. 

However, XRPL Foundation said the decision to skip the normal amendment process was made jointly by the Foundation, RippleX, core developers and validators after assessing the severity of the bug.

“No single party could make that call alone. Every validator and node operator chooses what software to run, and 3.4.1 only became required through a normal amendment vote with more than 80% validator support for two weeks. Protocol changes still go through amendments,” the foundation said. 

Related: Ledger confirms unauthorized hardware implant, says losses may exceed $86M

XRP Kuwait, an independent validator operator, also rejected claims that the coordinated upgrades signaled centralized control. 

“We disagree with the claim that operators coordinating an update is, in itself, proof of centralized control,” it said. “Coordination is not the same as control. Independent operators can assess a situation, communicate with one another, and reach the same conclusion without giving up their independence.”

Bug could have minted unlimited XRP 

The bug was an integer overflow in the XRP Ledger’s payment engine that had been present since 2015, according to the project’s vulnerability disclosure report. 

XRP balances are stored as 64-bit integers with a fixed maximum. When a sum exceeded that maximum, the calculation wrapped to a smaller number instead of failing. 

An attacker could exploit this by creating hundreds of specially priced offers, each asking for a very large amount of XRP, then sending one payment that consumed them all.

The engine would credit each offer owner their full amount but charge the buyer only the tiny wrapped total. The difference would be newly created, spendable XRP.

The attack required deliberately constructed offers and could not be triggered by normal trading activity, according to the report. Developers said they found no evidence that the issue was exploited on any public network.

title: XRP Gaining Nasdaq Exposure as Evernorth Takes 473M XRP Public
summary: Evernorth has completed its merger, bringing an actively managed XRP treasury to public markets ahead of expected Nasdaq trading. Its debut week will also feature a Times Square premiere celebrating the community behind the cryptocurrency. 473 Million XRP Moves Into a Public Company Stock market inv...
content:
Evernorth has completed its merger, bringing an actively managed XRP treasury to public markets ahead of expected Nasdaq trading. Its debut week will also feature a Times Square premiere celebrating the community behind the cryptocurrency.

Key Takeaways

  • Evernorth holds about 473 million XRP, with approximately $300 million in gross cash proceeds.
  • Common stock is expected to begin Nasdaq trading Oct. 12 as XRPN.
  • The Bearchamp finale is scheduled for Oct. 14 in Times Square.

473 Million XRP Moves Into a Public Company

Stock market investors are set to gain exposure to an actively managed XRP treasury after Evernorth Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: XRPN) completed its merger Oct. 9. XRPN is the ticker symbol for Evernorth’s common stock on Nasdaq. Its completed business combination brought together Evernorth and Armada Acquisition Corp. II, a special purpose acquisition company formed to take another business public.

At closing, Evernorth held approximately 473 million XRP and had raised approximately $300 million in gross cash proceeds before transaction expenses. Founder and Chief Executive Officer Asheesh Birla said:

“We’ll be deploying capital across the XRP economy, supporting the infrastructure and use cases that expand XRP’s utility, and pursuing strategies designed to grow XRP per share over time.”

Trading is expected to begin Oct. 12 following an administrative delay disclosed Oct. 6. The revised Nasdaq trading timetable replaced the earlier Oct. 8 target. Armada II previously used XRPN, with the symbol being reassigned to Evernorth following the merger.

Evernorth Targets More XRP Per Share

The transaction followed shareholder approval of the merger at Armada II’s Sept. 30 meeting. Evernorth’s investors include digital asset investment firm Arrington Capital, Japanese financial services group SBI Group, and Ripple. Other backers include blockchain investment firm Pantera Capital, crypto exchange Kraken, and GSR, a crypto trading firm and liquidity provider, among others.

That backing supports Evernorth’s plans to deploy capital across the XRP economy outlined Oct. 9 on X. The objective is to increase XRP per share, meaning the quantity of tokens held relative to outstanding shares. The business will operate under the reporting, governance, and disclosure standards of a Nasdaq-listed company.

Buying Evernorth stock gives investors an ownership interest in the company, which manages its treasury and business activities. Direct ownership of cryptocurrency recorded on a blockchain instead involves holding the digital asset itself. Evernorth plans to pursue returns through institutional and decentralized finance strategies, ecosystem participation, and capital markets activities. Decentralized finance refers to financial services conducted through blockchain-based applications.

Potential areas for investment include tokenized assets, blockchain-based credit markets, and settlement infrastructure on the XRP Ledger, the blockchain on which XRP operates. Tokenized assets represent ownership or other rights through digital tokens. Evernorth identifies these financial applications as areas that need funding to expand.

XRP Community Celebration Heads to Times Square

Evernorth’s public debut week will also bring the final chapter of its Bearchamp collaboration to Times Square in New York. Bearchamp is a boxing bear character created by Chicago artist JC Rivera. In an Oct. 10 update on X, the company scheduled the Times Square premiere for Oct. 14 at around 4 p.m. Eastern.

Rivera created the character after being discouraged from pursuing his childhood ambition to become a boxer. Evernorth introduced the character last month as part of its XRP community campaign tied to the Nasdaq debut. The initiative connects the character’s persistence with supporters who remained involved in the cryptocurrency’s ecosystem through years of setbacks.

The premiere will coincide with Evernorth’s planned Nasdaq closing-bell ceremony on Oct. 14, extending the celebration from the exchange to Times Square. Company leadership, investors, and members of the XRP ecosystem are expected to join the bell-ringing, according to its Oct. 9 release.

title: China Sees Explosive Growth of AI-Powered ‘One Person Companies’
summary: According to a recent report from the School of Journalism at Fudan University, by May 2026, there were 426 so-called One Person Company (OPC) communities registered in China, featuring the use of AI tools and run by entrepreneurs building solutions across several business fields. China rises as AI ...
content:
According to a recent report from the School of Journalism at Fudan University, by May 2026, there were 426 so-called One Person Company (OPC) communities registered in China, featuring the use of AI tools and run by entrepreneurs building solutions across several business fields.

Key Takeaways

  • China sees a boom in AI-driven micro-startups, with over 400 dedicated OPC communities nationwide.
  • Local governments offer computing subsidies to offset high operational and compliance costs for OPCs.
  • Experts urge Beijing to build supportive business ecosystems and maintain subsidies to sustain growth.

China rises as AI One Person Company Powerhouse

As it builds its national hardware stack, including humanoid AI-powered robots, China is also evolving its entrepreneurial landscape by using AI, and entrepreneurs are taking advantage of these solutions to advance small startups called One Person Companies (OPCs).

A report from a team at Fudan University’s School of Journalism revealed a rise in communities dedicated to developing these startups, reaching 426 across mainland China, covering 28 provincial administrative regions in 65 cities.

The report found that, while these communities have spread nationwide,they are largely concentrated in the eastern region, which offers clear advantages, as it has strong economic foundations consistent with high technological levels.

These companies fall into five different categories: campus incubation, enterprise experience transformation, scientific research, content creativity, and traditional business upgrade. These OPCs represent a new opportunity to revitalize the work ecosystem, allowing new companies to enter an already crowded business landscape and enabling new solutions and automation tools to rise in fields that were not considered by established companies.

Some areas in China have established stimulus for these companies. The Shanghai Pudong New Area provides up to 300,000 yuan in free computing power support for newly registered OPCs. Other areas have established entrepreneurship funds to help pay for computing costs, which constitute the largest share of the spending for these OPCs.

Compliance costs for these companies have also risen by up to 30% after the Data Security Law of the People’s Republic of China was implemented this year, increasing operational burdens for these structures. Nonetheless, this is deemed necessary, as their single-shareholder structure lacks traditional internal checks to prevent fund commingling and other potential criminal practices.

Even so, the number of these companies has been climbing significantly, with numbers reaching over 16 million businesses nationwide by June 2025.

The report concludes that to foster the survival of these companies, the government must build an ecosystem supporting them by forming archipelagos of these communities to achieve stable development, in addition to providing heavy subsidies.

title: Ledger attack spreads to EU, AI finds ’18 trillion XRP’ bug: Hodler’s Digest
summary: An user reports buying a tampered Ledger from a big retailer in Europe. Security researchers use AI to uncover a “$94 billion” XRP bug — but receive just a $250K bounty.
content:
Ledger implant exploit reportedly spreads to Europe after $93.4 million in losses from Asian reseller

A tampered Ledger attack that has already seen an estimated $93.4 million taken from Asian hardware wallet users, has reportedly spread to Europe.

X user Johannes has presented photographs of a tampered Ledger he said he purchased two weeks ago from the European consumer electronics chain MediaMarkt. The implant inside appears to be an earlier version of the one found linked to CryptoBilis shipped devices in Asia, and no funds have been taken.

“Either the device didn’t work, or they were waiting for a more widespread usage of the compromised devices,” he said. Former Mt Gox CEO Mark Karpeles, whose investigations into the tampered Asian Ledgers helped bring the problem to light, said the antenna in the device says it is the “Eurasian version” suggesting separate versions of the implant have been sent to regions that use different mobile frequencies. Ledger has not confirmed the reported European device is part of the same attack.

“PSA the ledger incident isn’t limited to Asia,” wrote European X user Johannes. Source: Johannes.

The sophisticated attack hit Ledger devices in Asia late last week, after devices from the official reseller CryptoBilis — which had recently been sold to a new owner — were found to be modified in a way that apparently enable attackers to read the seed phrase and steal funds even as though the device is still able to pass authenticity checks.

Ledger has asked CryptoBilis to suspend sales and shipments of its devices as a precaution and advised customers who had purchased devices from the reseller within the past 90 days to consider transferring their assets to a new Ledger. “The volume of impacted devices is limited,” it said in its most recent update today.

CryptoBilis is listed as an authorized Ledger reseller in Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines. Cybersecurity outlet Yfarmx estimated the losses at $93.4 million across 471 addresses, but this figure has not been confirmed by Ledger.

Security firm uncovers XRP minting bug

Security firm Veria Labs has been paid a $250,000 bug bounty for uncovering an overflow bug hidden in XRP’s code since 2015. It claims that a single transaction could have printed trillions of XRP out of thin air.  

The bug has been patched (amid some controversy) and there is no evidence it had ever been exploited.

Cayden Liao, Veria Labs security co-founder, wrote on X that its AI agent had combed through rippled, the software that runs the XRP Ledger and found two low severity bugs. It worked out how to create a much larger exploit by using them in conjunction. Liao said that just one exploit transaction could have created more than 18 trillion XRP, which is 184 times greater than the total supply.

“This puts the full $94B at risk, more than 60 times the largest crypto hack on record,” he wrote, referring to XRP’s entire market cap. “We suspect one reason nobody caught this vulnerability is that it chains together two bugs that would be low severity on their own.”  The bugs were reported on September 22 and RippleX patched them three days later.

Source: Cayden Liao

Vitalik Buterin backs crypto ‘bunker mode’ amid rapid AI math advances

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has backed researcher Justin Drake’s warning that advances in artificial intelligence could undermine the cryptography used in today’s blockchains before quantum computers do. 

“I don’t recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today,” Buterin wrote. “But we should take the risks to cryptography from AI-accelerated math seriously.”

Drake urged the industry to prepare for “bunker mode” in light of OpenAI releasing hundreds of new mathematical findings that humans have been unable to solve. None of the findings related to cryptography, but the potential for AI agents to uncover new insights into the mathematical structure behind elliptic curve cryptography or lattice based cryptography has the core Ethereum team worried.

The concerns have been criticized by other projects and analysts as fear mongering, with critics saying there is no evidence AI agents are anywhere near breaking cryptography. But then again, there wasn’t a lot of evidence a new AI model was about to one shot the solution to hundreds of other unsolvable problems either.

Samsung Wallet to add USDC transfers for US Galaxy users in October

Samsung plans to introduce USDC transfers to the Samsung Wallet payment app for 82 million eligible US Galaxy users in the last week of October.

The feature will let users send USDC to compatible crypto wallets internationally and transfer money to eligible bank accounts in more than 60 countries, where recipients can receive funds in their local currency. Users must complete identity verification to access the service.

Bastion will provide stablecoin account and payment infrastructure, with Coinbase serving as a sub-custodian through Coinbase Prime Vault. Solana and Sui were named as technical partners.

Crypto’s heavy backing of Republicans alienated Democrats: Cuomo

The crypto industry’s heavy backing of US Republicans has alienated Democrats whose support is needed to pass federal crypto legislation, says former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo.

Kalshi prediction markets put the probability of Democrats winning both chambers of Congress at about 61%. Cuomo said a Democratic-controlled Congress could either seek to roll back the SEC and CFTC’s crypto initiatives, or it could work with the Trump administration to pass the full CLARITY Act. 

“You need Democrats to pass the bill. You need Republicans. You have to be more balanced,” he said.

While he conceded there is a perception that Democrats are “anti-crypto” he says the technology fits in well with the party’s goals and beliefs.

“It’s empowering people who otherwise wouldn’t have access to financial products, and the Democratic Party has been working to do that all its life,” he said.

Winners and Losers

At the end of the week, Bitcoin (BTC) is down 2.8% to trade at $83,435, Ethereum (ETH) is down 6.5% to trade at $2,562 and XRP (XRP) is down 7% to $1.40. The total market cap is at $2.82 trillion according to CoinMarketCap.

Among the biggest 100 cryptocurrencies, the top three altcoin winners of the week are StarkNet (STRK) with a 91% gain (after announcing it would become a post-quantum L1), Binance Life (币安人生) on 25.4%, and Celestia (TIA) on 20.8%.

The top three altcoin losers of the week are Venice Token (VVV) which was down 18.5%, Sky (SKY) down 16.2% and Uniswap (UNI) down 15.4%.


Prediction of the Week

Ethereum will hit $25,000 to $50,000 this cycle says Tom Lee

Bitmine chair Tom Lee told Token2049 on Friday that ETH will top $5000 by the end of the year and by the end of the cycle Ethereum “could easily be 25,000 or 50,000 per token,” he said.

Lee also revealed Bitmine is nearing its 5% target after accumulating roughly 6 million Ether. The firm will only need to buy about 100,000 ETH more to reach that percentage.

“That’s a hard cap. We’re not gonna be accumulating past 5%,” Lee said. “We’re not gonna own more than 5% of Ethereum.”


Top FUD of the Week

Coldcard says it’s investigating how phishing link appeared on its X account  

Bitcoin-only hardware wallet Coldcard said an unauthorized phishing link appeared Sunday on its official X account, despite the company using offline two-factor authentication.

The post has since been deleted, and the firm said the only official website is https://coldcard.com. 

DefiLlama’s hack tracker estimated losses tied to July’s Coldcard exploit at $115 million.

THORChain dev accuses Tether of temporarily freezing USDT vaults

THORChain technical co-founder Chad Barraford accused stablecoin issuer Tether of blacklisting the network’s USDt (USDT) vaults without explanation, then unfreezing them hours later. 

In a Friday X post, Barraford said that Tether had blacklisted THORChain vault addresses, freezing about a combined 1.45 million USDT in the network’s funds across four wallets. He reported about two hours later than trading would resume after Tether unfroze all the addresses.

New York permanently bars Celsius founder Mashinsky in $35M fraud settlement

Former Celsius CEO Alex Mashinsky has been permanently barred from the cryptocurrency, securities and commodities industries under a settlement with New York Attorney General Letitia James that includes up to $35 million in conditional payments.

The New York agreement, announced Friday, settles a 2023 civil lawsuit accusing Mashinsky of misleading hundreds of thousands of investors about the safety of Celsius before its collapse in 2022.

Mashinsky is serving a 12-year federal prison sentence for fraud and was separately ordered to forfeit more than $48 million.


Top Magazine Features of the Week

France is world’s most dangerous place for Bitcoiners: 90 attacks in 7 months

French authorities recorded 90 crypto-related cases involving kidnapping, extortion, threats and violent theft in seven months. What makes France such a hotspot?

Crypto lending rises again… but have they solved the risks?

Crypto lending has risen by 55% since July, but now has to deal with the dangers of AI assisted hacks, and risks cascading through interlinked protocols. Here’s how to stay safe.

Capital starting to rotate back to crypto from AI: Raoul Pal

Real Vision founder Raoul Pal says a pause in the AI stock rally could help crypto attract capital, while AI agents are likely to boost Ethereum and Solana adoption.

title: Papertrade’s Wild Weekend Ends With 93.7% Open Interest Wipeout
summary: After a whirlwind of trading activity on Papertrade, the newly launched perpetuals decentralized exchange (DEX) built on Hyperliquid, the platform’s open interest has collapsed by 93.7% over the past 24 hours. The project’s total value locked (TVL) has also taken a substantial hit, shedding $48 mill...
content:
After a whirlwind of trading activity on Papertrade, the newly launched perpetuals decentralized exchange (DEX) built on Hyperliquid, the platform’s open interest has collapsed by 93.7% over the past 24 hours. The project’s total value locked (TVL) has also taken a substantial hit, shedding $48 million over the same period.

Key Takeaways

  • Papertrade’s explosive debut has taken quite a turn, with open interest plunging 93.7% from $11 billion to just $693 million in roughly 24 hours.
  • The exchange has also watched $48 million in deposits disappear, bringing its total value locked down from $118 million to $70 million after a whirlwind first weekend.
  • Beyond the disappearing billions, Papertrade is facing complaints over transaction priorities and attempted price manipulation, raising questions about whether the exchange can keep traders interested once the initial excitement wears off.

Papertrade’s $11 Billion Open Interest Craters as Deposits Flee

On Saturday, Bitcoin.com News examined the newly introduced perpetuals DEX, Papertrade.xyz, offering readers a closer look at the exchange’s underlying mechanics and trading structure.

The report highlighted Papertrade’s extraordinary 1,000x leverage and unconventional operating model, which distinguished it from competing perps platforms and prompted some observers to compare the trading experience to a “casino.” At the time, data compiled by paperdash.xyz placed Papertrade’s total value locked (TVL) at $118 million. As of Sunday, that figure has dwindled to $70 million, representing a $48 million contraction in the platform’s holdings.

When Bitcoin.com News initially examined the exchange, open interest stood at an eye-popping $11 billion, but that figure has since cratered by 93.7% to $693 million. Sunday’s figures further reveal that just $9.17 million is backing those outstanding positions.

Trading Complaints and Price Manipulation Attempts Test Papertrade

After its first full day of trading, Papertrade responded to a series of user grievances concerning the platform’s operations. Among the complaints, some traders expressed frustration that smaller transactions were not afforded the same priority as larger orders.

Papertrade defended the approach, explaining that indiscriminate transaction prioritization would have opened the door to thousands of minuscule orders overwhelming the system and exacerbating processing delays. Second, Papertrade acknowledged attempts by traders to manipulate bitcoin and ethereum prices.

According to the project’s statement on X, certain participants sought to exploit pricing data sourced from the perps DEX Hyperliquid, which Papertrade relies on to calculate the value of trading positions. This pricing mechanism is known as the best bid and offer (BBO).

In practical terms, it reflects the highest price a buyer is prepared to pay for an asset and the lowest price a seller is willing to accept. Papertrade maintains that some traders attempted to distort these quotations to extract profits from its exchange.

After the Frenzy, Papertrade Faces a Test of Staying Power

The project contends that such attacks were anticipated and accounted for during the six months devoted to developing its trading infrastructure. Papertrade’s first weekend has been a wild ride, with billions in trading positions disappearing, millions in deposits leaving the platform, and traders raising questions about how the decentralized finance (DeFi) operates.

While Papertrade insists its system was designed to handle manipulation attempts, the sharp decline in activity shows just how quickly enthusiasm can fade. For now, the bigger question is whether Papertrade can attract lasting interest once the initial excitement wears off, or whether its explosive debut will prove difficult to repeat. By the end of this report, TVL metrics dropped even lower to $67 million, according to paperdash.xyz.

title: DWF Labs Takes Bitgo to Court Over $141M Token Lock-up Dispute
summary: DWF Labs affiliates have taken cryptocurrency custodian Bitgo to London’s High Court, demanding $141 million over allegedly premature sales of discounted tokens. The plaintiffs claim Bitgo violated contractual lock-up restrictions by moving Falcon Finance (FF) and ESPORTS tokens onto exchanges rough...
content:
DWF Labs affiliates have taken cryptocurrency custodian Bitgo to London’s High Court, demanding $141 million over allegedly premature sales of discounted tokens. The plaintiffs claim Bitgo violated contractual lock-up restrictions by moving Falcon Finance (FF) and ESPORTS tokens onto exchanges roughly two months before their scheduled release. The alleged transactions placed selling pressure on thinly traded markets, leaving DWF-linked investment firms holding substantial positions that had lost considerable value.

Key Takeaways

  • DWF Labs affiliates are seeking $141 million from Bitgo over allegedly premature FF and ESPORTS token sales.
  • Bitgo allegedly moved discounted tokens to exchanges two months before their contractual lock-ups expired.
  • DWF Labs says the early sales damaged token prices, while Bitgo has declined to comment on the lawsuit.

Bitgo Faces $141 Million Legal Battle Over Alleged Token Lock-Up Violations

According to a report from the Financial Times (FT), the discounted cryptocurrency deal has turned into a $141 million courtroom fight, with DWF Labs affiliates accusing Bitgo of breaking its promise to keep certain tokens locked away. The dispute centers on private token purchases that allegedly came with a straightforward condition.

The institutional custodian Bitgo would receive the assets at reduced prices but could not sell or transfer them during an initial three-month lock-up period. Instead, the plaintiffs claim, tokens began moving onto exchanges roughly two months ahead of schedule, putting pressure on already fragile, illiquid markets and leaving the original sellers holding assets worth considerably less.

DWF Labs Accuses Bitgo of Breaking Its Lock-Up Agreements

The plaintiffs, DWF Maas and Falcon Digital, are investment vehicles associated with Dubai-based cryptocurrency market maker DWF Labs. Their lawsuit concerns private over-the-counter (OTC) transactions involving Falcon Finance’s FF token and ESPORTS, a cryptocurrency associated with the gaming sector.

Under the alleged agreements, Bitgo acquired discounted token allocations in exchange for accepting an initial three-month lock-up period followed by additional vesting restrictions. The reported arrangement was intended to prevent large amounts of cryptocurrency from entering circulation while DWF developed products and worked to improve market liquidity. But according to the lawsuit, Bitgo jumped the gun.

The plaintiffs allege that the custodian transferred or sold the tokens on exchanges approximately two months before the first scheduled unlock. DWF contends that those transactions introduced substantial selling pressure into markets characterized by limited liquidity and concentrated token ownership.

The lawsuit maintains there is “no contractual or other legal excuse for Bitgo’s conduct in transferring or selling” the tokens.

Token Prices Take a Beating as DWF Demands $141 Million

The financial fallout sits at the heart of the complaint. FF traded around $0.08 in early March 2026 before declining toward $0.07 by late April, according to historical market data. ESPORTS took a much harder hit, falling from approximately $0.28 in mid-March to $0.07 by early June. That represents a 75% decline over the period, although the extent to which Bitgo’s alleged transactions contributed to the drop remains disputed and has not been established in court.

DWF’s affiliates contend that the premature sales damaged the value of their remaining holdings. The plaintiffs are demanding $141 million in damages, including a reported $114 million component associated with losses on tokens they continued to hold. The firms argue that the discounted purchase prices were explicitly conditional on Bitgo honoring the agreed restrictions. Without those conditions, the plaintiffs maintain, the transactions would not have proceeded on the same terms.

DWF Says It Raised Concerns Months Before Filing Suit

The dispute reportedly began escalating in April and May 2026, when DWF representatives confronted Bitgo over the alleged transfers. The company says those discussions failed to produce satisfactory assurances, prompting its affiliates to pursue legal action.

“The discount Bitgo received was conditional on the tokens remaining locked, and they were moved to exchanges roughly two months before the first unlock. We raised this with Bitgo in April and May, and with no undertaking forthcoming, court action became necessary. We remain hopeful of, and open to, resolution,” DWF said in a statement reported by the Financial Times.

The case also arrives during a consequential year for the custodian, which made its New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) debut in January 2026 under the ticker BTGO. Its institutional custody and trading operations place the company squarely within the market for large cryptocurrency transactions and privately negotiated asset allocations.

A $141 Million Test of Crypto’s Private Token Deals

Beyond the substantial damages being sought, the lawsuit raises questions about how contractual restrictions are enforced when privately purchased cryptocurrency can move across exchanges and blockchain networks. Discounted OTC transactions are common in digital asset markets, allowing large investors to acquire substantial positions while giving token issuers and existing holders some control over when those assets enter circulation. Lock-up periods are central to those arrangements because they limit immediate selling pressure.

The London proceedings will examine whether Bitgo breached enforceable contractual obligations and whether the alleged transactions caused the financial losses claimed by DWF’s affiliates. For now, the accusations remain unproven, and no judicial determination has established that Bitgo violated the agreements or caused the reported price declines. DWF has indicated that it remains open to resolving the dispute outside court.

The bigger question is whether the plaintiffs can demonstrate that Bitgo’s alleged early transfers, rather than broader market conditions, were responsible for the losses behind their $141 million demand. Bitgo has not publicly responded to the lawsuit’s allegations or posted about it on any social media channels.

title: Keeper – Why Tonkeeper Went Multichain
summary: Nikita Monastyrskiy is chief marketing officer at Keeper, the self-custodial wallet formerly known as Tonkeeper. He started in crypto in 2018, running bounty and Bitcointalk signature campaigns while still at university, then spent four years at a crypto marketing agency, rising from community manag...
content:
Skip to content

Nikita Monastyrskiy is chief marketing officer at Keeper, the self-custodial wallet formerly known as Tonkeeper. He started in crypto in 2018, running bounty and Bitcointalk signature campaigns while still at university, then spent four years at a crypto marketing agency, rising from community manager to senior growth strategist. He went on to join the marketing team at Ethereum layer two Mode, helping take it from launch to exchange listings, before moving to Wallet in Telegram in 2025 as head of partner marketing. He later switched from the custodial side to the self-custodial one, joining Tonkeeper to lead its marketing.

The link will open a new window. Click the menu and down arrow to download the file.

Why you should listen

Tonkeeper built its reputation as the leading wallet on TON, and last month it gave up the name. Monastyrskiy explains why: users had stopped living on a single chain, and were juggling several apps to hold stablecoins on TRON, Bitcoin, Ethereum and assets on layer twos. The “TON” in the name tied the brand to one network, so the team dropped it and kept the rest. Keeper now supports seven networks, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, TRON and Base, and launched mobile-first, because that is where the data showed younger users transacting. 

He is direct about the trade-off at the heart of self-custody. Keeper cannot access, freeze or recover user funds, and he argues that the risk people associate with self-custody comes down to how they store their recovery phrase. Keep it offline and secure, and the main danger disappears. The harder part, in his view, is psychological: when an exchange gets hacked, users have someone to blame, but with self-custody the responsibility is entirely theirs. He sees the wallet as stage one of crypto adoption, the place where someone buys their first Bitcoin, and stage two as giving those users access to everything else on-chain, from tokenized stocks and prediction markets to simpler perpetual futures trading, which he says remains too complicated for newcomers.

Looking further out, Monastyrskiy describes his ideal wallet as one users barely see: connected to an AI assistant, taking voice commands to swap or trade, with no thought given to gas or withdrawals. He thinks a supervised version, where users still sign each transaction, is about a year away, and full automation further off. He also reports a pickup in on-chain activity since May, with volumes rising again this quarter. In the hot take round, he argues that real adoption will come from everyday payments in emerging markets rather than institutions, and picks Nineteen Eighty-Four as the science fiction he fears could become reality.

title: User Exposes Hidden Hardware Implant in European Ledger Wallet
summary: New social media reports indicate that physically exploited Ledger wallets may not be limited to Asia, with similar tampered devices reportedly found in Europe. The report comes as the company confirmed a hidden hardware implant in a wallet affected by the recent $93.4M exploit. New Tampered Ledger ...
content:
New social media reports indicate that physically exploited Ledger wallets may not be limited to Asia, with similar tampered devices reportedly found in Europe. The report comes as the company confirmed a hidden hardware implant in a wallet affected by the recent $93.4M exploit.

Key Takeaways

  • The $93.4M Ledger hardware wallet exploit has allegedly expanded to Mediamarkt, a major European retailer.
  • A customer found an earlier implant version that passes software checks, warning others to inspect devices.
  • Ledger claims the attack is limited to Asian reseller CryptoBilis but is now reviewing reseller controls.

New Tampered Ledger Wallets Allegedly Found Outside Asia

While the investigation into the recent $93.4M exploit that hit Ledger wallets sold in Asia by CryptoBilis, an authorized Ledger reseller, progresses, reports link the exploit to additional resellers in other regions.

Ledger has only acknowledged that a hidden implant was present in one of the devices affected by the million-dollar theft. Nonetheless, X user Johannes (4, 4) has presented evidence of more implants in another Ledger wallet reportedly purchased from Mediamarkt, a German chain of stores with a presence in several European countries, including Italy, Spain, Turkey, Poland, Austria, and the Netherlands, among others.

Johannes (4, 4), who allegedly acquired this wallet two weeks ago, pointed out that this implant seemed to be an earlier version, as it fails to hide the implant behind the device screen to make its detection difficult. Nonetheless, he explained that his wallet, while compromised, did not transfer his funds to the exploiter. “Either the device didn’t work, or they were waiting for a more widespread usage of the compromised devices,” he speculated.

Former Mt Gox CEO Mark Karpeles added that the antenna in this wallet read “Eurasian version,” hinting at different versions depending on the mobile frequencies used in each region.

Before, Mark Karpeles documented similar implants present in wallets sourced from Malaysia, where Cryptobilis is based. This new report expands the exploit to wallets offered in Europe, potentially exposing more customers to this attack vector.

Finally, Johannes (4, 4) recommended that Ledger owners who sourced their wallets from resellers open their devices and not trust Ledger’s software checks, as similar cases have appeared in other regions. All tampered devices passed Ledger software security checks, prompting customers to use them without concerns.

In its most recent update, Ledger clarified that all confirmed cases affected by this exploit were limited to devices sold through CryptoBilis, encouraging affected users to “reach out to Ledger Support through official channels and file complaints with their local law enforcement authorities.”

“We are continuously improving that work now and events like this strengthen our resolution: reviewing authorized reseller controls, advancing hardware protections, and cooperating with authorities,” Ledger concluded.

At the time of writing, Ledger Support has not addressed the swirling reports concerning alleged tampered devices stemming from European resellers.

title: Russia’s Moscow Exchange Pilots Crypto Trading for December Launch
summary: The exchange is currently testing its crypto trading capabilities with professional participants in a pilot environment that will escalate to full production before December. Boris Blokhin, Managing Director of Securities Market at the Moscow Exchange, stressed that the exchange’s current licenses a...
content:
The exchange is currently testing its crypto trading capabilities with professional participants in a pilot environment that will escalate to full production before December. Boris Blokhin, Managing Director of Securities Market at the Moscow Exchange, stressed that the exchange’s current licenses allow for this inclusion.

Key Takeaways

  • Russia’s Moscow Exchange plans to launch regulated cryptocurrency trading services on December 1.
  • Unqualified investors will face tight investment caps and be restricted to trading BTC, ETH, and USDT.
  • Officials expect the move to repatriate offshore funds, though 80% of volume may remain unregulated.

Moscow Exchange Announces Cryptocurrency Trading by December

The Moscow Exchange, Russia’s largest stock exchange, is preparing to enter the cryptocurrency era by offering trading services by December.

The company, which serves as a trading house for an equity market worth over $660 billion, is running a pilot test to prepare to add crypto trading services to its portfolio. On October 8, Boris Blokhin, Managing Director of Securities Market at the Moscow Exchange, stressed that the tests began a week earlier and that trading was expected to open on December 1.

“On December 1, we plan to provide such an opportunity to trade cryptocurrencies under the new legislation. Therefore, everything is very easy — both for the participants and for us, that is, we use the infrastructure of the stock market on which digital assets will be traded,” he stressed.

Blokhin reiterated that, under current regulation, the exchange would require no additional permits or licenses to offer these services.

The action follows the legalization of Russia’s cryptocurrency market after Bill No. 1194918-8 became effective on September 1, allowing Russian citizens to trade cryptocurrencies on national exchanges licensed by the Bank of Russia.

Nonetheless, the initial national rollout is expected to have limited reach, as unqualified investors will face investment limits that would cap the volume of funds entering the market, with their options restricted to three approved cryptocurrencies: Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Tether USDT. Conversely, qualified investors with a large risk profile will not be subject to these safeguards.

Even as the central bank has recently eased the requirements to become qualified investors, these limits are expected to affect the growth of the regulated national cryptocurrency market. Sberbank estimates indicate that crypto trading will reach at least 4 trillion rubles ($46.43 billion) in the first year, with only 20% going through exchanges; the remaining volumes will still be routed outside regulated channels.

According to Deputy Finance Minister Ivan Chebeskov, Russians hold nearly $44 trillion in crypto, mostly allocated in speculative investments and savings products outside the country. With regulation now in place, officials expect these assets to be repatriated, offering regulated venues and guarantees that were unavailable.

title: Everyone wants SCOTUS to take up prediction markets: State of Crypto
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court hasn't yet indicated whether it will take up cases surrounding prediction markets, but there are now several amicus briefs, an interim final rule and a rule proposal.
content:
Oct 11, 2026, 2:30 p.m. EDT

4 min read

A number of parties filed amicus briefs to the Supreme Court of the United States last week, urging it to take up a case on whether sports-based prediction market contracts are swaps, or not. And on Friday, the CFTC put out two proposals (one of which is now in effect) outlining its own thoughts on the matter.

You’re reading State of Crypto, a CoinDesk newsletter looking at the intersection of cryptocurrency and government. Click here to sign up for future editions.

Dodd: Frankly, no

The narrative

Former Senator Chris Dodd, former Commodity Futures Trading Commission (and Securities and Exchange Commission) Chair Gary Gensler, the National Football League, 39 states (and the District of Columbia), 145 tribal nations and various other parties filed amicus briefs to the Supreme Court urging it to take up this case, and with many arguing that sports-based prediction market products aren't swaps and shouldn't be regulated by the CFTC.

Why it matters

This newsletter covered the possibility of the Supreme Court wading into prediction markets a month ago. That calculus hasn't changed; there is now a major circuit court split, with two appellate courts ruling that prediction markets touching sports are actually gambling products that should be regulated by the states, and one appellate court ruling it's a CFTC issue.

Breaking it down

Most of the amicus briefs filed last week urged the Supreme Court to side with the states; that is, rule that at least sports-related prediction markets are actually gambling products that should be regulated at the state level and not the federal level.

Former Senator Chris Dodd, whose name appears on the 2010 Dodd–Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act at the center of this argument, said in a brief that the law was not intended to give the CFTC the authority to usurp state governments and their ability to regulate gambling.

The filing disagreed with the Third Circuit Court of Appeals panel which ruled 2-1 that the CFTC had jurisdiction over swaps and prediction markets covering sports, saying that there is a distinction between derivatives as financial instruments and sports wagers.

"Parlays that chain together multiple wagers — often on point spreads or player performances in different games, in different cities, in different sports — do not facilitate hedging or price discovery," the filing said, pointing to one example of sports-related prediction markets that have been popular. "Nor are they 'associated with' the type of 'potential financial, economic, or commercial consequences' required to qualify as swaps under the CEA."

Dodd's brief then took issue with the CFTC's argument that it has "exclusive jurisdiction" over these products.

"Nor is the CEA’s grant of 'exclusive jurisdiction' to the CFTC an express preemption provision immunizing every contract listed on a DCM from otherwise applicable state and tribal law. Rather, it identifies the CFTC as the federal regulator of covered financial instruments," his filing said.

Former CFTC Chair Gary Gensler, who also played a key role in drafting regulations implementing Dodd-Frank, similarly argued that the law did not grant the CFTC authority to preempt state gambling laws. He's made a similar argument in an appellate case as well.

The NFL argued it has a vested interest in the outcome of this case, given the importance of sports betting in, well, sports. The league took aim at what it described as the CFTC's "laissez-faire" approach to this issue, as well as the broader issue of there being a divergence in how states regulate gambling companies and how the CFTC regulates designated contract markets (the type of license prediction market providers have).

On Friday, the CFTC proposed an interim final rule and a separate proposal aiming to clarify its interpretation of how these products fall into the definition of a "swap." The agency said casino-style gambling falls outside its definition of a swap, but event contracts remain within it. And the regulator wants to formally include sports, politics, cultural and weather-related events as being part of event contracts that are counted as swaps.

Kalshi asked for, and was granted, an extension to file a response to the Supreme Court. Its deadline is now Nov. 9, 2026.

This week

This week

  • There are no Congressional hearings that we're tracking this week.

You can also join the group conversation on Telegram.

See ya’ll next week!

title: Bitcoin Price Eyes $85K, but Momentum Has Yet to Show Up
summary: Bitcoin’s price is holding near $83,770 on Oct. 11, 2026, after recovering from a recent low of $80,308, but the climb toward $84,000 is proving difficult. Short-term moving averages paint a mixed picture, while longer-term indicators remain largely positive. Oscillators suggest momentum has yet to ...
content:
Bitcoin’s price is holding near $83,770 on Oct. 11, 2026, after recovering from a recent low of $80,308, but the climb toward $84,000 is proving difficult. Short-term moving averages paint a mixed picture, while longer-term indicators remain largely positive. Oscillators suggest momentum has yet to catch up with the recovery, leaving bitcoin caught between improving technical conditions and resistance that continues to frustrate bullish ambitions.

Key Takeaways

  • Bitcoin’s price trades near $83,770, with resistance between $83,900 and $84,200 limiting its latest recovery.
  • Bitcoin’s RSI sits at 52, while negative momentum signals suggest the rebound still lacks confirmation.
  • Bitcoin remains above its longer-term averages, but losing $82,500 could expose the $80,308 low.

Bitcoin’s price is knocking on the door of $84,000, but the technical picture suggests the bulls haven’t quite found the key. Trading at $83,771.70, the leading cryptocurrency has advanced 0.9% over the past 24 hours, with its $1.683 trillion market capitalization reflecting a market that has recovered some ground without establishing a convincing breakout.

The latest readings reveal an interesting contradiction, as bitcoin trades above several important short-term exponential averages while remaining beneath comparable simple averages, creating a technical tug-of-war that could determine whether the recovery gathers momentum or runs out of steam.

Bitcoin’s Hourly Chart Tests the $84,000 Ceiling

The one-hour chart shows bitcoin consolidating between $83,700 and $83,800 after breaking away from an earlier trading range near $83,000. The advance followed a recovery from $80,308, with increased trading activity accompanying the initial move higher.

However, resistance between $83,900 and $84,200 remains a stubborn obstacle, and the latest price action has yet to establish a sustained foothold above that territory. A decisive move beyond $84,000 would bring $84,800 into focus, while another rejection could send bitcoin back toward $83,300 and eventually $83,000.

Four-Hour Chart Reveals Improving Structure

The four-hour chart offers a somewhat more encouraging interpretation, with a developing sequence of higher lows suggesting that bearish pressure has gradually eased since bitcoin retreated from $86,677. Nevertheless, the recovery remains incomplete, particularly as price continues to encounter resistance around $84,000.

Holding the $83,000 to $83,300 region would preserve the immediate recovery structure, while a retreat beneath $82,500 could expose $81,500. For now, the four-hour configuration suggests improving conditions rather than an established bullish reversal, with momentum still needing to confirm the price recovery.

Daily Chart Keeps the Bigger Picture in Perspective

The daily chart presents a more complicated story, as bitcoin remains below its recent $87,374 peak despite recovering from the $81,000 region. The broader sequence of lower highs has not been decisively broken, leaving the market vulnerable to another reversal if resistance continues to hold.

Still, bitcoin’s position above several longer-term moving averages suggests the underlying structure has not deteriorated significantly. Immediate support sits around $82,735, followed by the $82,500 region, while a deeper decline toward $80,900 would place additional pressure on the medium-term outlook.

Oscillators Expose Bitcoin’s Momentum Problem

The daily chart’s oscillator readings are predominantly neutral, with the relative strength index (RSI) registering 52 and Stochastic at 37. The commodity channel index (CCI) stands at negative 94, while the average directional index (ADX) reads 33, indicating meaningful trend strength without establishing its direction.

The Awesome oscillator (AO) registers 944, although momentum at negative 1,832, and the moving average convergence divergence (MACD) at 863 carry negative classifications. Meanwhile, the Stochastic RSI fast sits at 20, Williams at negative 61, the Ultimate oscillator (UO) at 42, and bull bear power at negative 1,158. Collectively, these figures suggest that bitcoin’s recovery has not yet generated convincing momentum confirmation.

Moving Averages Reveal a Divided Market

The moving averages (MAs) offer a particularly interesting contradiction. Bitcoin trades above its 10-period exponential moving average (EMA) at $83,503 and 20-period EMA at $83,193, but remains below the corresponding 10-period simple moving average (SMA) at $84,052 and 20-period SMA at $84,199.

The 30-period EMA at $82,253 and SMA at $82,472 provide additional support, while the 50-period EMA at $79,993 and SMA at $80,928 reinforce the longer-term positive structure. The 100-period and 200-period averages also remain comfortably below the market. Meanwhile, the volume-weighted moving average (VWMA) at $84,164 presents another immediate hurdle, leaving bitcoin sandwiched between improving support and stubborn overhead resistance.

Bull Verdict:

Bitcoin’s recovery remains constructive this weekend while price holds above $83,000, particularly with the 10-period and 20-period EMAs providing underlying support. A sustained advance through $84,200 would strengthen the bullish argument and potentially open the door toward $84,800 and $85,500. Clearing those levels would bring the previous $86,677 high back into consideration, although stronger momentum confirmation would make that scenario more convincing.

Bear Verdict:

Bitcoin’s inability to overcome the $83,900 to $84,200 resistance band leaves the recovery vulnerable to another setback. A retreat beneath $83,000 would weaken the immediate structure, while losing $82,500 could expose $81,500 and eventually the recent $80,308 low. With momentum and MACD still carrying negative classifications, the bearish argument cannot be dismissed, particularly while the daily chart continues to display lower highs.

title: Evernorth XRP Treasury Merger Brings 473 Million XRP to Nasdaq as XRPN Debuts October 12
summary: Evernorth has completed its SPAC merger with Armada Acquisition Corp. II, bringing 473 million XRP and $300 million in gross cash to its upcoming Nasdaq debut under ticker XRPN on October 12, 2026.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XRP

Evernorth has completed its SPAC merger with Armada Acquisition Corp. II, bringing 473 million XRP and $300 million in gross cash to its upcoming Nasdaq debut under ticker XRPN on October 12, 2026.

The transaction gives public-market investors another route to gain exposure to XRP through a company that actively manages its digital asset holdings. Backed by institutional investors including Ripple, Pantera Capital, Kraken, SBI Group, and Arrington Capital, Evernorth plans to allocate capital to XRP ecosystem infrastructure, decentralized finance (DeFi) strategies, and other initiatives intended to expand the token’s utility.

Evernorth Completes SPAC Merger With Armada Acquisition Corp. II

Evernorth announced the completion of its merger with Armada Acquisition Corp. II on October 9, marking its transition into the public markets. Armada, a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC), was sponsored by Arrington XRP Capital Fund, LP.

Evernorth completed its SPAC merger with Arrington XRP Capital-sponsored Armada Acquisition Corp. II, with Nasdaq trading under the ticker $XRPN scheduled to begin on October 12, 2026. Source: @evernorthxrp via X

Under the announced schedule, Evernorth common stock will begin trading on the Nasdaq Stock Market on October 12 under the ticker XRPN. The company also expects to participate in Nasdaq’s closing-bell ceremony on October 14, bringing together executives, investors, and members of the XRP ecosystem.

The merger establishes a publicly traded vehicle focused on managing an XRP treasury rather than simply holding the token as a passive reserve. Evernorth intends to combine digital asset exposure with the reporting, disclosure, and governance requirements associated with a Nasdaq-listed company.

Evernorth Enters Nasdaq With 473 Million XRP and $300 Million in Cash

At the close of the transaction, Evernorth held approximately 473 million XRP and raised around $300 million in gross cash proceeds before transaction expenses. The company said its investors include Arrington Capital, Ripple, Pantera Capital, Kraken, SBI Group, and GSR.

Evernorth will launch with approximately 473 million XRP and $300 million in cash, backed by major crypto investors and led by former Ripple executive Asheesh Birla. Source: @TheCryptoSquire via X

The combination of XRP holdings and cash gives Evernorth capital to manage its treasury and pursue investments across the broader XRP economy. However, the $300 million figure represents gross proceeds, not cash remaining after transaction costs or subsequent spending.

Evernorth is positioning itself as an institutional investment vehicle for people and organizations seeking XRP exposure through public equity markets. Investors buying XRPN shares will own stock in the company, not XRP directly. As a result, the share price may not move in exact proportion to XRP’s market price.

The company’s performance will also depend on its treasury management decisions, operating expenses, capital allocation, and ability to execute its business strategy.

Asheesh Birla Outlines Evernorth’s XRP Treasury Strategy

Evernorth CEO and founder Asheesh Birla said the company was established to support the XRP ecosystem while maintaining the transparency expected of a publicly traded business.

“In setting out to build Evernorth, our goal was to create something unique: an actively managed XRP treasury purpose-built to support the growth of the ecosystem with the transparency and governance that public markets demand,” Birla said in the October 9 announcement.

Evernorth CEO Asheesh Birla outlined a vision of tech-driven finance built on autonomous digital money and blockchain infrastructure as the company prepares to list on Nasdaq under $XRPN. Source: Asheesh Birla via X

The company intends to deploy capital across infrastructure, financial applications, and use cases designed to increase XRP’s utility. Its strategy also includes institutional and DeFi yield opportunities, ecosystem participation, and capital markets activities.

Evernorth has stated that it aims to grow the amount of XRP represented by each share over time. Achieving that objective will depend on investment returns, treasury management costs, changes in the company’s share count, and the performance of its holdings. The target is a stated business objective, not a guaranteed outcome.

Institutional Backing Supports Evernorth’s Public-Market Plans

Evernorth’s investor base includes several established participants in the digital asset industry. Ripple, Pantera Capital, Kraken, SBI Group, Arrington Capital, and GSR are among the institutions identified in the company’s announcement.

Michael Arrington, founder of Arrington Capital, said the firm’s support reflects its view that the XRP ecosystem can attract additional capital as it develops.

“Our conviction in XRP has always been rooted in the belief that the ecosystem would continue to mature, attracting serious builders and capital,” Arrington said.

Evernorth plans to direct capital toward areas such as tokenized assets, on-chain credit markets, and settlement infrastructure. These sectors require funding to develop products and expand their operations, although their commercial prospects and adoption rates remain uncertain.

Its public listing may make the company more accessible to investors who prefer traditional brokerage accounts over direct cryptocurrency ownership. However, stock market access does not eliminate the risks associated with digital assets, and investors will still face company-specific and market-related uncertainties.

What XRPN’s Nasdaq Listing Means for XRP Investors

Evernorth’s arrival on Nasdaq creates another publicly traded option for investors seeking exposure to the XRP ecosystem. Instead of purchasing and managing XRP themselves, investors can buy shares in a company whose treasury and strategy are closely tied to the token.

The distinction matters because XRPN shares and XRP are separate assets. The stock’s valuation will reflect not only the market value of Evernorth’s XRP holdings but also its cash position, liabilities, operating costs, investment results, and investors’ assessment of its future prospects.

XRP price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Evernorth’s strategy also introduces execution risks. DeFi activities can involve smart-contract vulnerabilities, liquidity constraints, and counterparty exposure. In addition, XRP price volatility could affect the value of its treasury and, in turn, investor sentiment toward its shares.

The company has cautioned that its business plans are subject to regulatory changes, market conditions, competition, and the risks of maintaining a public listing. Its future performance will depend on how effectively management navigates these challenges while pursuing its stated treasury objectives.

Evernorth expects to mark its public-market debut with a Nasdaq closing-bell ceremony on October 14, two days after the scheduled start of trading. The listing will put its active XRP treasury strategy under public-market scrutiny as investors assess whether the company can translate its substantial holdings and institutional backing into sustainable long-term value.

title: Saylor teases Strategy Bitcoin buying after ending September with STRC buybacks
summary: Investors will have to wait an extra day to find out if and how much Strategy added to its Bitcoin treasury in the first week of October.
content:
Strategy chair Michael Saylor teased investors watching Sunday for a signal of the company’s recent Bitcoin purchases with the message “There’s always room for more orange,” in a post on X.

However, any official notification via a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission won’t likely come before Tuesday, as federal offices will be closed on Monday for the Columbus Day holiday.

Strategy ended September by spending more than six times its weekly Bitcoin (BTC) buying budget on its repurchases of one of its preferred stocks. Strategy bought 334 Bitcoin (BTC) for $28.7 million between Sept. 28 and Oct. 4, bringing its holdings to exactly 848,000 BTC, according to an Oct. 5 8-K form.

Over the same period, Strategy repurchased about 1.77 million shares of its STRC preferred stock for $176.3 million.

Raise cash now, buy Bitcoin later

To be sure, Strategy’s recent moves could be read as an indication that management can build up cash now and spend it on BTC later.

Independent analyst Shanaka Anslem Perera on Saturday noted that Strategy raised $5.41 billion from new common shares in the third quarter and ended the period with 1,666 more BTC than it held at the end of June.

In his monthly newsletter on Bitcoin and crypto, Perera wrote that Strategy’s SEC filings “allocate 9.5% of the raise directly to bitcoin purchases. Other disclosed uses included a dollar reserve, cash, dividends and preferred-share buybacks.”

“The question for investors is what the financing left behind. For a shareholder, bitcoin per share is only part of the answer. Cash counts too, while debt and preferred shares have claims ahead of common stock,” he wrote.

“During the third quarter Strategy raised billions through share sales, but much supported cash reserves and preferred shareholders. Raising capital does not necessarily mean buying bitcoin,” he told Cointelegraph on Sunday.. 

“That does not mean they stopped buying BTC. Cash retained can fund later purchases, and strengthening the balance sheet can benefit shareholders.”

title: Clarity's failure could speed crypto innovation while shielding incumbents
summary: Executives see openings for tokenization, DeFi and dealmaking, while lawyers warn agency action leaves spot-market oversight and lasting certainty unresolved.
content:
Oct 11, 2026, 12:00 p.m. EDT

4 min read

Summary

  • SEC and CFTC initiatives could expand regulated onchain trading and institutional access.
  • Legal experts expect gradual progress, with gaps Congress must address.
  • Executives see opportunities for DeFi, but established exchanges could retain their competitive advantage.

The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act’s failure to advance in the Senate has shifted the next phase of U.S. crypto regulation to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), opening prospects for more trading and investment to move onchain while leaving a central question unresolved: how much certainty can regulators deliver without Congress?

Interviews with senior executives and legal experts suggest broad agreement that regulation will keep moving. Their expectations diverge over whether agency action can become a durable foundation or leave businesses adapting to rules vulnerable to political and legal change.

Lev Breydo, an assistant professor of law at William & Mary Law School, said Clarity exposed divisions within the industry, from ethics provisions to the yield fight with community banks.

“A coalition that looked unified against Gensler found out definitions create winners and losers,” he said.

Despite the setback, agencies are moving quickly to fill the regulatory gap.

The SEC’s five-year “Innovation Exemption” introduced September 17 lets qualifying venues trade tokenized U.S. stocks through blockchain liquidity pools while it works on permanent rules.

The CFTC followed on October 5, seeking feedback on rules for leveraged retail crypto trading and a new registration category for crypto markets. That starts a lengthy public comment and rulemaking process, rather than putting rules into effect.

Meanwhile, the SEC’s October 1 custody proposal would let state trust companies safeguard client crypto and allow advisers and funds to hold it themselves under certain conditions.

Looking into 2027, Breydo said he expects the SEC to focus on completing offering and custody rules and building on its tokenized-stock exemption. He sees the agencies’ March joint interpretive release as an important foundation, superseding earlier guidance and allowing coordination within existing law.

But a key gap remains: ordinary, unleveraged spot trading still lacks comprehensive federal oversight, beyond the CFTC’s anti-fraud and anti-manipulation powers. Closing that gap was a central goal of Clarity.

More activity, sooner

For some executives, the legislative setback could produce faster commercial opportunities.

“The SEC and CFTC are already moving proactively to provide the regulatory certainty markets need, and that’s unlocking a wave of M&A across digital assets, traditional financial services, and fintech alike,” said Paul McCaffery, head of digital assets at investment bank KBW.

Bitwise Chief Investment Officer Matt Hougan said he sees the agency approach as more favorable in the short term than legislation that would have required years of follow-up rulemaking. He also expects more protocols to adopt token buybacks, particularly buy-and-burn models, following SEC clarification he said gives investors greater confidence.

Developers are watching whether regulators distinguish writing software from running a financial intermediary. Cathy Yoon, chief legal officer at Solana-focused research and development firm Temporal, said she hopes the SEC will recognize developers as software creators without turning their work into a securities enterprise.

“The fact that the SEC staff is even willing to say these things explicitly is a win,” Yoon said, while noting staff FAQs are not SEC rules.

Michael Lie, global head of digital assets at market maker Flow Traders, said he sees comprehensive regulation as inevitable as finance moves toward 24/7 trading. He is watching innovation exemptions and changes to transfer-agent rules, with European and Asian regimes already advancing.

The durability test

Legal experts see progress arriving in stages, with implementation the hardest part.

“The biggest gap is implementation,” said Derek Lowrey, head of legal at Newton Labs (formerly known as Magic Labs). Without legislation, overseeing venues, intermediaries, decentralized finance (DeFi) and spot markets remains harder, he said. Existing anti-money laundering, sanctions and record-keeping obligations nevertheless give compliant teams a basis to keep building.

Kevin Kreuser, general counsel at domain-name tokenization firm D3, said tokenized real-world assets particularly need clearer jurisdictional boundaries.

“Agency action is welcome, but it does not provide the same long-term certainty as legislation,” he said.

Jim Petrila, chief legal officer at Dromos Labs, which develops Aerodrome and Velodrome, takes a more bullish view: growing liquidity and tokenized securities on public blockchains could make reversal impractical within two years.

“For DeFi, the signal is bullish,” he said.

Still, the benefits may be uneven. Hougan argued Clarity's failure preserves a regulatory moat for Coinbase (COIN), Kraken and other incumbents, delaying competition that could lower costs. The emerging outlook is faster experimentation, but unresolved questions over who can compete and how firmly the new rules will hold.

Breydo said only Congress can deliver a comprehensive framework with statutory durability.

title: IMF finds demand for tokenized stocks, says the market is still volatile, illiquid
summary: Investors are using blockchain-based shares for smaller and after-hours trades. The IMF says liquidity, legal rules and settlement systems have not caught up.
content:
Oct 11, 2026, 9:00 a.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • Tokenized U.S. stocks offer round-the-clock trading and fractional ownership, with more than half of trades occurring outside regular market hours and about 80% involving less than one share, the IMF found.
  • Overnight price moves carried useful information, with more than 85% reflected in conventional shares within five minutes of markets opening.
  • The IMF said tokenized equities remain a small, fragmented market that could improve settlement and automation, but require stronger legal, liquidity and interoperability safeguards.

Tokenized stocks are already delivering two of crypto’s long-promised benefits: round-the-clock trading and the ability to buy a fraction of a share. They are also markedly less liquid and more volatile than the conventional equities they track, according to a new International Monetary Fund (IMF) study.

The IMF’s latest Global Financial Stability Report, titled Scaling Tokenization: New efficiencies and new vulnerabilities, examines the five most actively traded tokenized U.S. equities, including Tesla (TSLA), Nvidia (NVDA) and Alphabet (GOOG) as well as measures such as the Nasdaq 100 Index, across centralized and decentralized venues.

More than half of trading took place outside regular U.S. market hours, the IMF found. About 80% of trades were for less than one share. For the report, those figures are evidence that investors value 24/7 access and lower entry points, not just the technology behind a tokenized stock.

The study also found that overnight moves in tokenized stocks carried useful information for the underlying shares. Once U.S. markets opened, more than 85% of the overnight movement in tokenized shares was reflected in their traditional counterparts within five minutes, the IMF said.

“Moving assets onchain is only the first step," said Bitget CEO Gracy Chen. "The bigger question is how efficiently that capital can work once it is there.”

The IMF’s message is that while the use case is real, the market is still nascent. It said the tokenized real-world asset (RWA) market has grown rapidly, estimating it at about $65 billion as of July 31. Tokenized equities accounted for roughly $2.3 billion of the total. That compares with a 2025 global equity market capitalization of just under $160 trillion, according to the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association (SIFMA), the trade group for the U.S. securities industry.

Still, the tokenization project is growing. Bullish (BLSH), a Gibraltar-based crypto company and CoinDesk’s parent company, introduced tokenized equity trading in August. Earlier this month, OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), which owns and operates the New York Stock Exchange, filed plans for a venue offering round-the-clock trading in tokenized U.S. shares.

They are not alone. Crypto exchanges Coinbase Global (COIN), Kraken and Binance also offer tokenized stock trading, as does Robinhood Markets (HOOD).

According to the IMF, tokenized stocks were about 1.5 times as volatile as the equivalent shares on traditional venues and significantly less liquid.

The problem is not simply that blockchain markets are small. Tokenization needs enough issuers, investors, trading venues and settlement assets on compatible systems to deliver its promised savings in cost and time. Today’s market is split across private platforms, public blockchains, custodians and settlement tools that often do not work together.

The IMF said tokenization could replace some of the manual work firms do to reconcile records, automate tasks such as dividend payments and speed up collateral transfers. It warned that automated margin calls and liquidations, collateral moving between platforms and 24-hour trading could make a market shock harder to contain.

The risks are still small because tokenized markets remain small, the IMF said. But its report argues that legal rules on ownership, safeguards for liquidity, links between systems and settlement arrangements need to be developed before the market grows much larger.
